nodes.name: Monday 03:15 IST
nodes.notes: Weekly, not daily. The Apify account is a $5/month free plan and the digest is a weekly read; a nightly run would multiply noise without multiplying signal.

nodes.name: 0. Discover organisers (free)
nodes.notes:
Walks the Eventbrite and MeraEvents organiser sitemaps — a plain fetch, no actor and no credits, which is why it runs here rather than on a button. Turning a *name* into a domain is the part that bills, and that stays at POST /api/resolve behind an admin session.

limit is 100, and the ceiling is Cloudflare rather than the server: MeraEvents needs one page fetch per profile, so limit=50 measured 28s and limit=400 exceeded Cloudflare's ~100s edge timeout — the request returned empty while the run carried on to completion server-side. That failure mode is the bad one, because n8n logs a failed node for work that actually succeeded. Raise this only against POST /api/discover, which is not behind the proxy timeout in the same way.

nodes.name: 1. Scan (free collectors only)
nodes.notes: There is deliberately no free_only parameter to set. The endpoint forces it: paid collection belongs on a button with its price on it, not on a cron that bills at 3am. Passing free_only=false here does nothing.

nodes.name: 2. Classify complaints
nodes.notes: MUST run before drafting, and this is the node most likely to be moved by someone tidying the flow. Every draft is written about the complaint pattern for the platform a company runs, and that pattern is computed from the columns this step fills. Put it after drafting and each week's drafts are written from the previous week's evidence — which still produces plausible output, so nothing would look broken.

nodes.name: 3. Enrich companies
nodes.notes: Apollo organizations/enrich, which works on the free plan. This is company enrichment, not the paid people/match — that one is per-row and admin-only, and never runs here.

nodes.name: 4. Draft outreach
nodes.notes: Billed in LLM tokens. Ten at a time on purpose: drafts are meant to be read before they are sent, and a hundred unread drafts is the same as none. The response carries generic_pitch — true means nobody has replaced the placeholder value proposition and every draft this week inherited it.

nodes.name: 5. Reconcile Apify spend
nodes.notes: Compares what we recorded against Apify's own monthly figure. Our number is what the spend cap reads, so a drift between the two means the cap is guarding the wrong total.

nodes.name: 6. Alerts
nodes.notes: Catches the two failures the queue cannot show you: a collector that stopped returning, and a cron that stopped firing. Empty response means healthy.

nodes.name: 7. Weekly digest (text)
nodes.notes: Plain text, ready to paste into email or WhatsApp. Add a send node after this one — it is left unwired because where the digest should go is a decision, not a default.

meta.notes: Every step here is free or LLM-token-billed. No node in this workflow can trigger a paid collector: /cron/scan forces free_only server-side, and the paid paths (Trustpilot, G2, Apollo people/match) are admin-only POSTs to /api/* that require a browser session. That separation is the point — free work on a schedule, paid work on a click. Set the Authorization header on all seven HTTP nodes to `Bearer <MCP_BEARER_TOKEN>` from .env.prod before activating.
